concept_use.Basic geometry about circle: The angle in a segment is constant and the chord subtends twice that angle at the centre; inside the circle the angle is larger. This fixes the region and r = 2 sqrt 3.

english: Let $A=(-3,0)$ and $B=(3,0)$. Let $R$ be the set of all points $P(x,y)$ with $y>0$ for which $\angle APB\geq\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Then the area of the region $R$ is
hindi: माना कि $A=(-3,0)$ तथा $B=(3,0)$ हैं। माना $R$ उन सभी बिन्दुओं $P(x,y)$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $y>0$ तथा $\angle APB\geq\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ है। तब क्षेत्र $R$ का क्षेत्रफल है
solution: Points above $AB$ seeing $AB$ at exactly $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ lie on an arc of a circle through $A,B$; inside that circle the angle is larger, outside it is smaller
Angle at the centre $=2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so $r=\dfrac{AB}{2\sin(\pi/3)}=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}}=2\sqrt{3}$, centre $(0,\sqrt{3})$ (above $AB$)
$R$ is the major segment above the chord $AB$, whose central angle is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
solution_full: By the angle-in-a-segment theorem, all points on one side of $AB$ that see $AB$ under a fixed angle $\alpha$ lie on an arc of a circle through $A$ and $B$.

A point inside that circle (on the same side) sees $AB$ under a larger angle, and a point outside under a smaller angle. So for $y>0$ the condition $\angle APB\geq\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ means that $P$ lies inside or on the circle, above $AB$.
The chord $AB=6$ subtends $2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ at the centre $O_{1}$, so $AB=2r\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, giving $r=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}}=2\sqrt{3}$.

The centre lies on the perpendicular bisector $x=0$ at distance $\sqrt{r^{2}-9}=\sqrt{3}$ from $AB$. For the arc above $AB$ to see $AB$ at an acute angle, the centre is on the same side, so $O_{1}=(0,\sqrt{3})$.
Hence $R$ is the part of the disc $x^{2}+(y-\sqrt{3})^{2}\leq12$ with $y>0$, that is, the major segment cut off by the chord $AB$.

The minor segment (below $AB$) has central angle $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and area $\dfrac{r^{2}}{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}-\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)=6\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=4\pi-3\sqrt{3}$.
originality_note: New: a region defined by an angle inequality (way 2, a set defined by a construction) that turns out to be a major segment of a circle. Closest known: locus of a point seeing a fixed segment under a fixed angle (an arc). Different because: the inequality and the half-plane must be translated into a region and its area needs the major segment, not the arc.

Checked that y > 0 removes the lower circle, and that points on AB itself are excluded by y > 0 (area unaffected). Answer 8 pi + 3 sqrt 3 at (C) as planned. No change.
key_step: Recognise that {angle APB >= pi/3, y>0} is the major segment of the circle through A, B with r = 2 sqrt 3, then segment area.
justification: Two routine circle facts (angle at centre, segment area) chained, plus the translation of an inequality into a region; no non-standard idea. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q2 (L2) in demand.
